ragas.name: Yaman
ragas.aroha: N R G m P D N S'
ragas.avroha: S' N D P m G R S
ragas.time_of_day: First quarter of the night (approx. 6 PM – 9 PM)
ragas.description: One of the most important ragas in Hindustani classical music. Uses all seven notes with tivra (sharpened) Ma as the most characteristic note. Considered a raga of the evening with a calm, expansive character. The raised fourth (tivra Ma) immediately distinguishes it from related ragas.

ragas.name: Bhairav
ragas.aroha: S r G M P d N S'
ragas.avroha: S' N d P M G r S
ragas.time_of_day: Early morning (Brahma muhurta, approx. 4 AM – 6 AM)
characteristic_phrases: P d P M G r
ragas.description: A morning raga of great antiquity and gravitas. Uses komal (flattened) Re and Dha, giving it a deeply introspective and devotional quality. The name is associated with Lord Shiva. Its characteristic slow, meditative movements make it one of the most revered ragas for early morning performance.

ragas.name: Bhairavi
ragas.aroha: S r g M P d n S'
ragas.avroha: S' n d P M g r S
ragas.time_of_day: Morning; traditionally the closing raga of a concert
characteristic_phrases: S' n d P M g r S
g M P d n d P
ragas.description: Uses all five komal (flattened) swaras: Re, Ga, Dha, Ni, with shuddha Ma and Pa. Despite its modal heaviness, it conveys both pathos and devotion. It is traditionally performed as the last piece of a concert. In practice, additional notes are sometimes used for expressiveness, making it one of the more flexible ragas.

ragas.name: Malkauns
ragas.aroha: S g M d n S'
ragas.avroha: S' n d M g S
ragas.description: A pentatonic raga (no Re or Pa) using komal Ga, Dha, and Ni. The absence of Pa and the prominent use of all three komal notes gives it a dark, mysterious, and meditative quality. It is considered one of the most powerful ragas in the Hindustani tradition and is associated with late-night performance.

ragas.name: Bhupali
ragas.aroha: S R G P D S'
ragas.avroha: S' D P G R S
ragas.description: A pentatonic raga (no Ma or Ni) from the Kalyan thaat. Despite its simple structure (only 5 notes), it has great scope for melodic development. Its notes are all shuddha (natural), giving it a serene, pleasant character. It is easily accessible and often used for devotional and light classical compositions.

ragas.name: Darbari Kanada
ragas.aroha: S R g M P d n S'
ragas.avroha: S' n d P M g r S
characteristic_phrases: n d P M g r
ragas.description: One of the grandest and most elaborate ragas in Hindustani music, traditionally attributed to Miyan Tansen (court musician of Emperor Akbar). Uses komal Ga, Dha, and Ni. Its most characteristic feature is the slow, oscillating meend (glide) on the komal Ga and the distinctive movement around komal Dha. Requires considerable expertise to render correctly.

ragas.name: Bageshree
ragas.aroha: S g M D n S'
ragas.avroha: S' n D M g R S
ragas.description: A raga of the Kafi thaat, using komal Ga and Ni. It omits Re in the ascent, giving the ascent a characteristic pentatonic quality. It is associated with themes of longing and separation (viraha). The combination of komal notes and the characteristic avoidance of Re in the aroha gives it a unique, slightly plaintive colour.

ragas.name: Asavari
ragas.aroha: S R M P D S'
ragas.avroha: S' n d P M g R S
characteristic_phrases: n d P M g R
ragas.description: Uses different notes in ascent and descent (vakra/crooked movement). The ascent uses shuddha Dha while the descent uses komal Ga, Dha, and Ni. This asymmetry is a key identifying feature. It has a serious, slightly melancholic character and is traditionally an early morning raga.
